summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a model catalog demo focusing on selecting open models, benchmark profiles, and compatibility matrices for AtlasMed's inference workload. AtlasMed is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deploys; main concerns are latency for clinical workflows, cost, and data residency/SOC2. Next steps: share deck, run a 2-week POC benchmark, and align on security docs and network requirements.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Ivy Chen (Redwood Product), Hannah Ortiz (AtlasMed Head of ML), Dr. Ravi Chandran (CTO), Maya Torres (SRE), Omar Nadeem (Data Engineer)

Summary (auto): Quick tour of Redwood model catalog, demos of selecting open models and filter by benchmark/compatibility; discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs and private deployment constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Laura from Redwood, quick land acknowledgement, Marcus will run through the model catalog demo and Ivy will jump in on product questions. 
[00:18] Hannah: Hi all, thanks, we're excited; quick note we have a clinical workflow that's pretty latency sensitive for triage so that's the main ask.
[00:30] Marcus: Got it, we'll focus on latency and then show the compatibility matrix for private and dedicated. Also we'll surface benchmarks per model. 
[01:10] Dr. Ravi: Quick intro, our stack is in GCP, we have a mix of CPU and A100 dedicated in our lab, and some HIPAA constraints — primarily want audit logs and KMS.
[01:35] Laura: Perfect, those are common. We'll show SOC2 stuff and the KMS integration later; Ivy will have the security links.
[02:05] Marcus: Opening the model catalog now, so top-left you can filter by task — generation, chat, embeddings, rerank — and then by model family and compute profile. I'm going to filter to open Llama-family variants and a couple of Mistral checkpoints for comparison.
[03:00] Marcus: Notice the benchmark column, we surface two profiles: latency p95 for a 512 token context and cost per 1k tokens with default batching. These are synthetic but based on our internal runner and per-hardware profiles. 
[03:35] Omar: Are those numbers from hosted infra or normalized?
[03:45] Marcus: Good question, they're normalized to hardware class and quantization level; there is a note that the absolute may vary; for exact numbers we'll run a benchmark in a POC on your env.
[04:20] Hannah: Can we see a compatibility matrix? We have an LLM abstraction in our infra that expects certain kv cache behaviors and streaming support.
[04:40] Marcus: Sure, switching to the compatibility tab — it lists runtime features like streaming, kv cache offset compat, tensor shapes, supported quant formats (q4_0, q8, etc.), and also deployment compatibility (hosted, dedicated, private). For example, this Llama-2-70B-ggml variant supports streaming and kv cache but only on x86 with CUDA + cutlass kernels; the q4_0 path is only for our dedicated pool or private where you bring the right kernel.
[05:35] Dr. Ravi: So does the catalog tell us which kernel version we need for our A100s?
[05:50] Marcus: Yes it has a 'recommended kernel' column — for A100 we recommend smash-1.2 cutlass kernels with our runtime; for some open quant formats we fallback to a slower path.
[06:30] Maya: Our security team cares about private control plane and audit logs; do we need to run Private deployment on-prem for HIPAA or can we do VPC?
[06:50] Ivy: You can do VPC Private — our Private option supports customer-managed networking (VPC peering) and KMS integration. On-prem is optional if you need air-gap. Both produce full audit logs and RBAC.
[07:25] Hannah: How does routing/fallback work — if a model variant isn't available will requests fallback to another model?
[07:40] Marcus: Yes, the smart routing layer has policy-based fallbacks. You can pin to model versions and also set compatible fallbacks (e.g., smaller quantized variant) to preserve latency SLOs. We demo that in the console.
[08:20] Laura: Let's demo picking two open models and compare their benchmarks side-by-side.
[08:35] Marcus: Selecting Mistral-7B-refined and Llama-2-13B-instruct — you can toggle context length to 2k tokens and we recalc p95 latency. Here you can see the Mistral is lower latency on default quantization but slightly lower score on our internal eval for instruction accuracy.
[09:10] Hannah: What are the evals? Can we upload our own eval set?
[09:22] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports custom evals and will run quality regressions tied to prompt sets; we show eval scores per model and can do A/B testing during rollouts.
[10:00] Omar: How accurate are the transcription notes that power these evals? (laughter)
[10:05] Laura: (laughing) The transcript might be spotty, but the eval harness uses your ground truth.
[10:25] Marcus: Back to cost — the catalog shows recommended quantization profiles and estimated cost. If you pick q8_0 or q4_0 the per-token cost drops substantially but you might see some accuracy delta. We also show a suggested batching policy for each model based on common latency distributions.
[11:05] Hannah: For clinical triage we can't tolerate hallucinations; how do we monitor quality?
[11:20] Ivy: We recommend conservative eval thresholds, and Redwood Optimize can alert on regressions tied to specific prompt sets. You can also enable deterministic sampling and lower temperature for inference.
[12:00] Dr. Ravi: About throughput — we have peak loads during morning batch, can your dedicated pools Autoscale quickly?
[12:20] Marcus: Dedicated pools have configurable autoscaling and burst capacity; autoscale depends on GPU provisioning time but we keep warm spare capacity. For sub-second scale you can use caching or smaller pinned instances to maintain tail latency.
[13:05] Maya: On the Private side, what's required for peering? Any network ports?
[13:20] Ivy: We'll send a network checklist; generally you need to allow outbound to control plane endpoints for management (optionally on-prem disconnected mode) and some gRPC ports for the runtime. We'll include specifics in the security doc.
[14:00] Marcus: Now demoing the compatibility matrix export — you can CSV download which lists models, supported quant formats, recommended kernel, supported sequence lengths, and whether streaming is supported. Useful for your infra team to map to their LLM adapter.
[14:40] Omar: Can we automate selection? Like if latency SLO is 200ms and cost target is X, can Redwood pick the variant dynamically?
[14:55] Marcus: Yes, you can create routing policies with cost/latency priorities, and Redwood will pick the best model variant based on runtime profiles and recent telemetry. The Console shows simulation results for policy changes.
[15:30] Hannah: What's the difference between hosted ranges and dedicated regarding data retention?
[15:40] Ivy: Hosted API has configurable retention windows and opt-out for training pipelines; Dedicated and Private give you stronger isolation and full control over logs — enterprise packages include longer retention and audit logs.
[16:15] Marcus: I'm going to show the API example — simple REST call: model: "redwood/mistral-7b-q4_0", streaming true, and function calling is supported on top of models that have structured output support.
[16:50] Dr. Ravi: Does function calling require particular model features?
[17:00] Marcus: It requires the model to produce structured tokens reliably; we mark models in the catalog as 'structured-friendly' based on evals.
[17:30] Hannah: Any notes on quantization toolchain — can we bring our own quantized models?
[17:45] Marcus: You can bring your own model artifacts in Private deployments; for hosted we onboard verified quantized variants. If you bring your own, we run a compatibility pass and may recommend kernel changes.
[18:20] Omar: How are KV cache semantics handled across model families?
[18:35] Marcus: We surface cache semantics per model — some older open checkpoints use a different KV layout; our runtime has shims for many formats, listed in the compatibility matrix. In private you can add additional shims.
[19:10] Hannah: For the POC we want to run a 2-week benchmark with our real prompts and traffic; what telemetry will we get?
[19:25] Marcus: You'll get token-level latency, per-request cost estimates, error rates, and per-prompt quality metrics if you enable evals. We can give a dashboard with traces and slow request samples.
[20:00] Laura: Let's talk timeline and procurement — is Dedicated monthly commitment or annual?
[20:12] Ivy: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits; we can propose a pilot or a trial with limited commit for POC.
[20:40] Dr. Ravi: Security question — do you support SSO/SAML for the Console and RBAC?
[20:52] Ivy: Yes SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC with role templates, and audit logs. KMS/HSM integrations for key wrapping are supported in Private and Dedicated.
[21:25] Hannah: Any known gotchas with our GCP + Anthos setup?
[21:40] Marcus: Anthos is fine for Private; the main thing is ensuring kernel compatibility on GPU nodes and network peering for control plane connectivity. We'll add a note in the checklist.
[22:10] Omar: A practical question: do we need to change our embedding service to use Redwood embeddings or can we host our own?
[22:25] Marcus: You can keep your embedding pipeline; Redwood can call out to it or you can host embedding models in the Private deployment. Catalog supports embedding-specific metrics too.
[23:00] Laura: Demoing Optimize suggestions — this is where we recommend batching/prefix cache settings and quant profiles per workload. For interactive low-latency you may prefer smaller batch sizes and enable prefix caching for repeated prefixes.
[23:45] Hannah: We've got a lot of repeated prefixes in triage, sounds promising. How much does prefix caching help?
[24:00] Marcus: It depends on reuse rate; in our benchmarks we often see 20-40% token reduction for high prefix reuse, which translates directly to cost savings and latency improvements.
[24:30] Dr. Ravi: About fallback policies — if a large model is down do calls fall back to a smaller model automatically in-flight?
[24:45] Marcus: Yes, you can configure immediate fallback to a compatible model variant; there may be minor API differences but we try to keep tokenization and response shape consistent.
[25:20] Maya: For the POC we'll need an isolated dataset. Can Redwood promise not to use our logs for training?
[25:35] Ivy: For Dedicated/Private we provide contractual guarantees — Hosted has opt-out but we can sign agreements for data handling. We'll include the data residency and training opt-out language in the docs.
[26:10] Omar: Any checkpoint names we should avoid because of license?
[26:25] Marcus: The catalog has license flags; some community checkpoints have restricted terms and we mark them as non-commercial or require attribution. We'll send the CSV.
[27:00] Hannah: Could you show the side-by-side A/B rollout flow?
[27:15] Marcus: Demoing rollouts — you pick a new model version, define cohorts, and Redwood will do canary deployment with automatic rollback on quality regressions. You can tie rollback thresholds to your eval metrics.
[28:00] Laura: Let's address cost — what ballpark numbers should we expect for high-availability low-latency triage at 100 qps?
[28:15] Marcus: Quick back-of-envelope: depends on model and quantization — Mistral-7B q4_0 on dedicated could be X per hour (we use placeholder in demo) while a 13B may be 2-3x. We'll run exact numbers in the POC benchmark with your traffic.
[29:00] Dr. Ravi: We need specifics for budget to take to procurement.
[29:10] Laura: We'll provide a pricing sheet and a POC estimate; Marcus will include estimated GPU hours and expected token costs.
[29:45] Hannah: For the POC, we'd like Redwood to run the benchmark in our VPC with a dedicated instance and then compare against your hosted numbers.
[30:00] Marcus: That's our standard POC pattern, we'll send the config and script.
[30:25] Maya: Any special firewall rules?
[30:35] Ivy: Minimal — will share a network checklist, mainly control plane endpoints and optional outbound egress for telemetry.
[31:10] Omar: On a technical note, can we lock model weights or pin a version so results are reproducible?
[31:25] Marcus: Yes, you can pin model versions and we snapshot model artifacts for Dedicated and Private to guarantee reproducibility.
[32:00] Laura: Quick pause for questions.
[32:10] Hannah: One more — can Redwood run a benchmark that includes our eval metric (F1 on entity extraction)?
[32:20] Marcus: Absolutely, bring the eval set and we'll run it in the POC and tie alerts to any regression.
[33:00] Dr. Ravi: Does Redwood handle data masking or PII redaction in transit?
[33:12] Ivy: We have options for PII redaction and can integrate with your pre-processing; also recommend client-side tokenization to avoid storing PHI in logs.
[33:50] Marcus: Back to the console — showing the compatibility CSV export and the per-model kernel recommendation. I'll attach a demo link after the call.
[34:30] Omar: A question on deployment time — if we need to spin up a dedicated pool how long?
[34:45] Ivy: Depends on cloud, typically a few hours to provision if capacity is available; initial setup for Dedicated/Private has a few configuration steps.
[35:15] Hannah: For procurement we'll need SOC2, ISO docs and contractual language for data processing.
[35:25] Laura: We'll include those in the follow-up bundle.
[36:00] Marcus: Demoing Optimize: it flags that for your triage workload it recommends q4_0 on 13B for accuracy but q8_0 on 7B for latency; you can configure a policy to prefer accuracy during night and latency during peak.
[36:40] Hannah: That policy switch sounds useful. Will that happen automatically?
[36:50] Marcus: You can schedule or set triggers based on observed latency or cost thresholds.
[37:20] Dr. Ravi: Any special considerations for HIPAA compliance?
[37:30] Ivy: We'll provide our compliance pack — typically Dedicated or Private is preferred for PHI, coupled with customer-managed KMS and audit retention.
[38:10] Omar: Are there limits to API throughput per account?
[38:20] Marcus: Rate limits are configurable for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has tiered limits but we can set higher quotas for enterprise customers.
[39:00] Laura: Wrapping up the demo, attaching the model catalog export and compatibility matrix to the meeting notes.
[39:20] Hannah: Thanks, this was helpful. We'll review with procurement and security.
[39:40] Dr. Ravi: Please send pricing and security docs.
[39:55] Laura: We'll send pricing, the CSV export, and the security checklist; Marcus will draft the POC plan.
[40:20] Marcus: For the POC we'll run your prompt set for two weeks in your VPC, capture latency and quality, and give a final report.
[40:50] Maya: Timeline — we can aim for a kickoff the week of 2026-03-16.
[41:05] Laura: I'll propose two times in calendar after the call.
[41:30] Hannah: Anything else on the product side?
[41:40] Ivy: Just to note, we'll include kernel compatibility notes for your A100 fleet.
[42:00] Omar: Thanks all.
[42:10] Laura: Quick recap of next steps: send deck + pricing (Laura), security & network checklist (Ivy), POC plan and benchmark script (Marcus).
[42:30] Hannah: Sounds good.
[42:40] Dr. Ravi: Thank you.
[42:50] Laura: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments.
[43:00] End of call.
